`scripts/project.py`:

```py
"""One entry point for local setup, regeneration and native builds."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOLS = ROOT / 'vendor/ps3recomp/tools'

def config():
    p = ROOT / 'config/local.json'
    if not p.exists(): raise SystemExit('Run: python scripts/project.py setup --elf YOUR_ELF --disc YOUR_PS3_GAME --ffmpeg YOUR_FFMPEG')
    result=json.loads(p.read_text())
    return {k: (ROOT / v).resolve() for k,v in result.items()}

def run(args, **kwargs):
    subprocess.run([str(x) for x in args], cwd=ROOT, check=True, **kwargs)

def logged_run(args, log_path, **kwargs):
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    print('Diagnostics:', log_path, flush=True)
    with log_path.open('wb') as output:
        result = subprocess.run([str(x) for x in args], cwd=ROOT,
                                stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, **kwargs)
    if result.returncode:
        # Preserve the entire log; show a bounded tail for immediate diagnosis.
        with log_path.open('rb') as source:
            source.seek(max(0, log_path.stat().st_size - 8000))
            print(source.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
        raise SystemExit(f'Build failed ({result.returncode}); full log: {log_path}')

def build_environment():
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if os.name != 'nt': return env
    vswhere=Path(os.environ.get('ProgramFiles(x86)','C:/Program Files (x86)'))/'Microsoft Visual Studio/Installer/vswhere.exe'
    install=subprocess.check_output([str(vswhere),'-latest','-products','*','-requires','Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64','-property','installationPath'],text=True).strip()
    if not install: raise SystemExit('Visual Studio C++ build tools are required')
    vcvars=Path(install)/'VC/Auxiliary/Build/vcvars64.bat'
    task=ROOT/'temp/vcvars.cmd'; task.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    task.write_text(f'@echo off\ncall "{vcvars}" >nul\nif errorlevel 1 exit /b 1\nset\n')
    output=subprocess.check_output(['cmd','/d','/c',str(task)],text=True)
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if '=' in line and not line.startswith('='):
            key,value=line.split('=',1); env[key]=value
    clang=Path(install)/'VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/clang-cl.exe'
    if not clang.is_file(): raise SystemExit('Install Visual Studio LLVM/clang-cl tools')
    env['MV_CLANG']=str(clang)
    return env

def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__); sub=ap.add_subparsers(dest='cmd',required=True)
    s=sub.add_parser('setup'); s.add_argument('--elf',required=True); s.add_argument('--disc',required=True); s.add_argument('--ffmpeg',required=True)
    s.add_argument('--keys-dir', default='game/private_keys', help='Private headers and optional keys.json')
    b=sub.add_parser('build'); b.add_argument('--jobs',type=int,default=8); b.add_argument('--configure-only',action='store_true')
    g=sub.add_parser('generate'); g.add_argument('--stage',choices=['ppu','spu'],required=True); g.add_argument('--jobs',type=int,default=8)
    sub.add_parser('check')
    args=ap.parse_args()
    if args.cmd=='setup':
        c={'elf':str(Path(args.elf).resolve()),'disc':str(Path(args.disc).resolve()),'ffmpeg':str(Path(args.ffmpeg).resolve()),'keys':str(Path(args.keys_dir).resolve()),'userdata':'game/userdata','generated':'build/generated/named'}
        for key in ('elf','disc','ffmpeg'):
            if not Path(c[key]).exists(): raise SystemExit(f'Missing {key}: {c[key]}')
        with Path(c['elf']).open('rb') as source:
            if source.read(4) != b'\x7fELF':
                raise SystemExit('Supply a decrypted ELF, not a SELF/container')
        if not (Path(c['disc'])/'USRDIR').is_dir():
            raise SystemExit('--disc must be the matching PS3_GAME directory containing USRDIR')
        for directory in ('include','lib','bin'):
            if not (Path(c['ffmpeg'])/directory).is_dir():
                raise SystemExit(f'FFmpeg development distribution missing {directory}/')
        (ROOT/'config/local.json').write_text(json.dumps(c,indent=2)+'\n'); print('Local configuration saved (Git-ignored)'); return
    if args.cmd=='check': run([sys.executable,ROOT/'scripts/check_repository.py']); return
    c=config()
    if args.cmd=='generate':
        if args.stage=='ppu':
            out=c['generated']/'ppu'
            if out.exists() and any(out.iterdir()): raise SystemExit('Existing lift preserved. Move it to temp/ before regeneration.')
            meta=ROOT/'build/metadata'; meta.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            run([sys.executable,TOOLS/'ppu_loader.py',c['elf'],'--output',meta])
            functions=meta/'named.functions.json'
            run([sys.executable,ROOT/'scripts/analysis/debug_elf_functions.py',c['elf'],'--out',functions])
            run([sys.executable,TOOLS/'ppu_lifter.py',c['elf'],'--functions',functions,'--hle-stubs',meta/(c['elf'].stem+'.imports.json'),'--cpp-nonlocal-jumps','--output',out,'--jobs',args.jobs])
        else:
            images=ROOT/'build/extracted/spu'; out=c['generated']/'spu'
            if out.exists() and any(out.iterdir()): raise SystemExit('Existing SPU tree preserved. Move it to temp/ before regeneration.')
            run([sys.executable,TOOLS/'extract_spu_images.py',c['elf'],'--output',images])
            run([sys.executable,TOOLS/'build_spu_workloads.py','--images',images,'--lifted',out,'--out',out/'spu_workloads.c','--title','MotorStorm MV','--constructor'])
        print('Generated output is private and ignored. See docs/BUILDING.md for additional module requirements.'); return
    if args.cmd=='build':
        if not 1<=args.jobs<=8: raise SystemExit('Use 1..8 jobs to bound compiler memory')
        if os.name=='nt':
            # Required discipline before relinking. No matching process is harmless.
            subprocess.run(['taskkill','/F','/IM','ms1_recomp.exe'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        env=build_environment(); binary=ROOT/'build/native'
        command=['cmake','-S',ROOT,'-B',binary,'-G','Ninja','-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug','-DPORT_CPP_NONLOCAL_JUMPS=ON',f'-DRECOMP_DIR={c["generated"]/"ppu"}',f'-DSPU_DIR={c["generated"]/"spu"}',f'-DPS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_ROOT={c["ffmpeg"]}',f'-DPORT_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR={c.get("keys",ROOT/"game/private_keys")}']
        if 'MV_CLANG' in env: command.extend([f'-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER={env["MV_CLANG"]}',f'-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER={env["MV_CLANG"]}'])
        logs=ROOT/'temp/builds'/datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S.%fZ')
        logged_run(command,logs/'configure.log',env=env)
        if args.configure_only: return
        logged_run(['cmake','--build',binary,'--parallel',args.jobs],logs/'build.log',env=env)
        exe=binary/('ms1_recomp.exe' if os.name=='nt' else 'ms1_recomp')
        identity={'path':str(exe),'sha256':hashlib.sha256(exe.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'bytes':exe.stat().st_size,'elf_sha256':hashlib.sha256(c['elf'].read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'ppu_tree':str(c['generated']/'ppu'),'spu_tree':str(c['generated']/'spu'),'logs':str(logs)}
        (binary/'build_identity.json').write_text(json.dumps(identity,indent=2)); print('Build identity:',identity['sha256'])

if __name__=='__main__': main()
```

`scripts/run.py`:

```py
"""Muted native run with unique output ownership and resource guards."""
import argparse, ctypes, datetime, hashlib, json, os, subprocess, time
from pathlib import Path
import psutil
from project import ROOT, config

class Memory(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_=[('length',ctypes.c_ulong),('load',ctypes.c_ulong)]+[(x,ctypes.c_ulonglong) for x in ('total_phys','available_phys','total_commit','available_commit','total_virtual','available_virtual','available_extended')]

def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__); ap.add_argument('--seconds',type=int,default=600)
    capture=ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    capture.add_argument('--capture-havok',action='store_true',help='Existing Havok plus graphics/audio diagnostic profile')
    capture.add_argument('--capture-havok-only',action='store_true',help='Enable only the existing Havok observer, without graphics/audio probes')
    ap.add_argument('--capture-bike',action='store_true',help='Prepare bike observer; arm with the owned bike/arm.txt before observed input')
    args=ap.parse_args()
    if not 1<=args.seconds<=600: raise SystemExit('Bounded run must be 1..600 seconds')
    if any(p.info['name']=='ms1_recomp.exe' for p in psutil.process_iter(['name'])): raise SystemExit('A native instance already exists; close it first')
    c=config(); exe=ROOT/'build/native/ms1_recomp.exe'
    if not exe.is_file(): raise SystemExit('Build first: python scripts/project.py build')
    out=ROOT/'temp/runs'/datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S.%fZ'); out.mkdir(parents=True)
    env=dict(os.environ)
    # Clear inherited diagnostics before applying the documented booting configuration.
    for key in list(env):
        if key.startswith(('SPU_','FLOW_','RSX_','GCM_','PAD_','FPS_','PM_','CAP_HAVOK','CAP_BIKE','AUDIO_')) or key in ('FP_PICK','SCREEN_AS_TEX','RD_WWSJOB_SHIM'):env.pop(key)
    env.update(PATH=str(c['ffmpeg']/'bin')+os.pathsep+env.get('PATH',''),PS3_VFS_ROOT=str(c['disc']),PS3_HDD0_ROOT=str(c['userdata']),PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT=str(c['userdata']/'home/00000001/savedata'),AUDIO_MUTE='1',SPU_PM_INTERP='1',SPU_PROBE_INTERP='0',SCREEN_AS_TEX='0',PAD_FILE=str(out/'pad.txt'),FPS_STATS='1',FPS_STATS_CSV=str(out/'frames.csv'),RECOMP_TITLE='MotorStorm MV native')
    for key in ('SPU_WP','SPU_PM_GATE_TRACE','SPU_PM_RETIRE_GUARD','SPU_PM_PC_RESUME','SPU_PM_FLOW_RESUME','SPU_PM_YIELD_RESUME'):env[key]='0'
    env['PS3_KEYS_FILE']=str(c.get('keys',ROOT/'game/private_keys')/'keys.json')
    if args.capture_havok or args.capture_havok_only:
        (out/'havok').mkdir(); env['CAP_HAVOK_DIR']=str(out/'havok')
    if args.capture_havok:
        (out/'rsx').mkdir()
        env.update(VDEC_TRACE='1',FP_PICK='036CC2C1',RSX_DBG_VP='04E6FD00',RSX_DBG_VTX='04E6FD00',RSX_DBG_CB='04E6FD00',AUDIO_RATE='1',RSX_PHASE_STATS='1',RSX_PHASE_CSV=str(out/'rsx_phases.csv'),SPU_INTERP_STATS='1',AUDIO_PEAK='1',AUDIO_WAV=str(out/'audio.f32'),PM_JOBPARAMS='1',PS3_FSLOG='1',RSX_CAP='110:3:20',RSX_CAP_DIR=str(out/'rsx'))
    if args.capture_bike:
        (out/'bike').mkdir()
        env.update(CAP_BIKE_DIR=str(out/'bike'),CAP_BIKE_ARM_FILE=str(out/'bike/arm.txt'),PS3_FSLOG='1')
    (out/'pad.txt').write_text('0\n')
    log=(out/'native.log').open('wb');err=(out/'native.err').open('wb')
    p=subprocess.Popen([str(exe),str(c['elf'])],cwd=ROOT,env=env,stdout=log,stderr=err,creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
    proc=psutil.Process(p.pid); start=time.monotonic(); reason='guard tooling failure'; terminated=False
    record={'pid':p.pid,'create_time':proc.create_time(),'exe':str(exe),'exe_sha256':hashlib.sha256(exe.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'elf_sha256':hashlib.sha256(c['elf'].read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'output':str(out),'muted':True,'capture_havok':args.capture_havok or args.capture_havok_only,'capture_bike':args.capture_bike,'capture_profile':'broad' if args.capture_havok else 'havok-only' if args.capture_havok_only else 'none','environment':{k:v for k,v in env.items() if k in ('PS3_VFS_ROOT','PS3_HDD0_ROOT','PS3_SAVEDATA_ROOT','AUDIO_MUTE','PAD_FILE','CAP_HAVOK_DIR','CAP_BIKE_DIR','CAP_BIKE_ARM_FILE','SPU_PM_INTERP') or k.startswith('SPU_PM_') or k=='SPU_WP'}}
    (out/'launch.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)); print('Owned native PID',p.pid,'output',out,flush=True)
    try:
        while p.poll() is None:
            elapsed=time.monotonic()-start; m=Memory();m.length=ctypes.sizeof(m)
            if not ctypes.windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx(ctypes.byref(m)):raise OSError('Memory guard unavailable')
            private=proc.memory_info().private
            with (out/'resources.jsonl').open('a') as f:f.write(json.dumps({'elapsed':elapsed,'private':private,'physical_available':m.available_phys,'commit_available':m.available_commit})+'\n')
            if (out/'stop.txt').exists():reason='explicit stop marker';break
            if elapsed>args.seconds:reason='bounded duration elapsed';break
            if private>14*1024**3 or m.available_phys<4*1024**3 or m.available_commit<12*1024**3:reason='resource limit reached';break
            time.sleep(2)
        else: reason='guest process exited; inspect logs for outcome'
    finally:
        if p.poll() is None:
            terminated=True;p.terminate()
            try:p.wait(timeout=10)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:p.kill();p.wait(timeout=10)
        record.update(reason=reason,elapsed=time.monotonic()-start,returncode=p.returncode,terminated_by_guard=terminated)
        (out/'final.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2));log.close();err.close();print('Closed:',reason,flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

`scripts/spu/lift_flash_codec_at_base.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lift a flash codec SPU ELF at a FIXED staging (link) base.

flashATRAC / flashMP3 stage themselves into SPURS task LS at runtime-chosen
bases (MS1 flashATRAC: 0x32880, 0x33880, 0x2F780).  The stock module lift is
module-relative (base 0): its labels, links and data absolutes are module
offsets, so it can only be served by the interpreter at a runtime base.
A lift built at base B runs natively exactly like the PM jobmods' link-base
0x4000 lifts: spu_lifter.py --auto-functions <elf> --base B moves every
function bound, label and registration address to B+off (vendor change), and
ila-encoded extern hops keep their original low-LS SPURS targets.

Usage:
  python lift_flash_codec_at_base.py --elf build/spu-inputs/flashATRAC.elf \
      --base 0x32880 --prefix flashATRAC_b32880 --code-end 0x7DC0 \
      --out build/generated/named/spu/flashATRAC_b32880 \
      --module-lift build/generated/named/spu/flashATRAC/spu_recomp.c

--module-lift (optional): the original module lift.  Its extern stub targets
are read and restored in the generated source if the base shift biased any
relative-encoded (brsl) extern call.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE    = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TOOLS   = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(
    HERE, "..", "..", "vendor", "ps3recomp", "tools"))


def debase_includes(path):
    """Rewrite '../../../runtime/spu/x.h' includes to bare 'x.h' so the TU
    builds from any tree (same rewrite build_spu_workloads.py applies)."""
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        txt = f.read()
    new = re.sub(r'#include\s+"(?:\.\./)+runtime/spu/([A-Za-z0-9_]+\.h)"',
                 r'#include "\1"', txt)
    if new != txt:
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(new)


def module_extern_stubs(module_lift_c):
    """Extern stub targets from the original module lift:

    void <p>spu_func_XXXXXXXX(spu_context* ctx) {
        ctx->pc = 0xXXXXXXu; g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; ... }

    A stub's own address and its ctx->pc target match in the module lift."""
    stubs = set()
    pat = re.compile(
        r"void\s+\w*spu_func_([0-9A-Fa-f]{8})\(spu_context\* ctx\)\s*\{\s*"
        r"ctx->pc = 0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)u;\s*g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch;")
    with open(module_lift_c, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for m in pat.finditer(f.read()):
            if int(m.group(1), 16) == int(m.group(2), 16):
                stubs.add(int(m.group(1), 16))
    return stubs


def fix_extern_stubs(out_c, base, externs):
    """Restore original extern targets the base shift biased.

    Every extern hop in these codecs is a RELATIVE branch: under the base
    shift the disassembler computes base+target and masks it to 18 bits
    (0x3FFFF), so a target like 0x164C0 lands at (base+0x164C0)&0x3FFFF.
    Rewrite the stub name and its ctx->pc back to the original target --
    the externs live in the host task's fixed low-LS SPURS area and must
    NOT follow the codec's staging base."""
    with open(out_c, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        txt = f.read()
    fixed = 0
    for a in sorted(externs):
        biased = (base + a) & 0x3FFFF
        name_old, name_new = f"spu_func_{biased:08X}", f"spu_func_{a:08X}"
        fixed += txt.count(name_old)
        txt = txt.replace(name_old, name_new)
        for pc_old, pc_new in ((f"ctx->pc = 0x{biased:X}u", f"ctx->pc = 0x{a:X}u"),
                               (f"ctx->pc = 0x{biased:X};", f"ctx->pc = 0x{a:X};")):
            fixed += txt.count(pc_old)
            txt = txt.replace(pc_old, pc_new)
    with open(out_c, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(txt)
    return fixed


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--elf", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--base", required=True, help="staging base, e.g. 0x32880")
    ap.add_argument("--prefix", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--code-end", default=None,
                    help="passed through: trims data-tail pseudo-functions")
    ap.add_argument("--module-lift", default=None,
                    help="original module lift spu_recomp.c (extern stub source)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = int(args.base, 0)
    cmd = [sys.executable, os.path.join(TOOLS, "spu_lifter.py"),
           "--auto-functions", args.elf,
           "--base", hex(base),
           "--symbol-prefix", args.prefix + "_",
           "--output", args.out]
    if args.code_end:
        # --code-end is expressed in MODULE space; the base shift moves the
        # bounds past it, so hand the lifter the shifted address.
        cmd += ["--code-end", hex(base + int(args.code_end, 0))]
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    for fn in os.listdir(args.out):
        if fn.endswith((".c", ".h")):
            debase_includes(os.path.join(args.out, fn))

    if args.module_lift:
        externs = module_extern_stubs(args.module_lift)
        fixed = 0
        for fn in ("spu_recomp.c", "spu_recomp.h"):
            fixed += fix_extern_stubs(os.path.join(args.out, fn), base, externs)
        print(f"extern stubs restored: {fixed} (targets "
              f"{', '.join(hex(a) for a in sorted(externs))})")
    print(f"lifted {args.elf} at base 0x{base:X} -> {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`scripts/spu/lift_ms1_debug_dsp.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""lift_ms1_debug_dsp.py -- reconstruct + lift the DEBUG-vintage mstream DSP
modules from staged local-store dumps.

The debug EBOOT (EBOOT_MSMVdbgUS.ELF) does NOT embed the six mstream DSP
.pic modules (its only embedded SPU images are spu/msngSPURS and
hkspursconstraint), and the beta disc (BCJS-30004) carries no
audio/110/pic/ directory -- the debug runtime's "audio/110/pic/mstream_dsp_"
path is unsatisfiable from anything on disk. The ONLY debug-vintage bytes in
existence here are the staged images captured in the probe-miss LS dumps:

    temp/captures/spu_staged_miss_2F010.bin
        window LS [0x2EC10, 0x37010)   (branch target 0x2F010 - 0x400)
        -- the only capture that covers the compressor PT_LOAD in full.

Staging model (validated on the capture): the loader places .pic file[0x100:]
at LS base+0x80, so [base, base+0x80) holds stale bytes; the PT_LOAD is
followed by the 12-byte ELF-note header (namesz 8, descsz 0x20, type 1),
the SPUNAME self-naming note and the .shstrtab names, all inside the
observable region. The .pic CRT carries a position probe
(`ila $r2, <module_rel(own+4)>; brsl $r79, .+4; sf $r79,$r2,$r79`) --
the ila immediate calibrates each module base exactly (cross-checked
against the retail compressor: ila 0xA8 for the brsl landing at 0xA8):

    compressor  base 0x2EF80  load [0x2F000,0x2FD00) fsz 0xD00
                (note header verified at 0x2FD00; probe fn at 0x2F430 =
                base+0x4B0 with ila 0x4B8)
    reverb      base 0x2FD00  load [0x2FD80,0x31F00) fsz 0x2180 entry +0xA0
                (probe fn at 0x2FDA0 = base+0xA0 with ila 0xA8)

GCC vintage 4.0.2 (CELL 4.1.11, $Rev: 1035 $) -- distinct from the retail
EBOOT's embedded GCC 4.1.1 Rev 1826 modules (already lifted, ids 3-8 in
the retail tree). The remaining four (distortion/eq/filter/IR) have no
bytes on disk anywhere; they stay interpreter-served until a run stages
them (the probe-miss dumper captures them at their bases).

Observed runtime branches into the staged compressor (img 1):
    0x2F430 = +0x4B0  lr 0x03C50 (runtime call -- primary entry)
    0x2F808 = +0x888  lr 0x043D0 (runtime call)
    0x2F010 = +0x090  lr 0x2F95C (internal brsl from +0x9D8)
    0x2F340 = +0x3C0  lr 0x2F974 (internal brsl from +0x9D0)
A probe only matches a pc when implied base (pc - entry) == lift_base, so
each first-branch offset that img 1 can jump to gets its own companion
probe over a shifted (but module-internal) fingerprint window; after the
first hit the resident-code slot covers the whole span and later internal
branches dispatch natively without probing.

This script:
  1. slices the PT_LOAD + note tail out of the dump for each module,
  2. rebuilds a .pic-shaped SPU ELF (ehdr + 3 phdrs + PT_LOAD@vaddr 0x80 +
     PT_NOTE) under ignored build/spu-inputs/images_dbg/,
  3. lifts each module module-relative (--base 0, ids 14/15) and per
     observed staging base (--base 0x2EF80 / 0x2FD00, ids 20/21) into explicitly
     supplied target-specific trees, seeding every
     observed branch target via --extra-funcs,
  4. prints the register_stage_probe lines (fingerprints are FNV-1a-64
     over the staged PT_LOAD slice -- exactly what the runtime hashes),
  5. removes stale per-base DSP dirs from previous (wrong-base) runs.

Usage:
    python lift_ms1_debug_dsp.py --dump PATH --trees DIR[,DIR]
"""

import argparse
import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TOOLS = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "vendor", "ps3recomp", "tools"))
LIFTER = os.path.join(TOOLS, "spu_lifter.py")

IMAGES_DBG = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "build", "extracted", "debug_dsp")

DUMP_BASE = 0x2EC10          # LS address of dump byte 0

def fnv1a64(b):
    h = 1469598103934665603
    for x in b:
        h = ((h ^ x) * 1099511628211) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h

# name, module base (LS), PT_LOAD start (LS), PT_LOAD size, .pic e_entry
# (module off), extra function seeds, probe entry offsets.
# The staged blob is file[0x100:] at base+0x80: PT_LOAD, then the 12-byte
# ELF-note header, then name/desc. The note header words sit at load+fsz,
# so the observable region ends 0xC past the true PT_LOAD end. Sizes below
# are the true fsz values (dump end minus 0xC).
MODULES = [
    dict(name="mstream_dsp_dbg_compressor", base=0x2EF80,
         load=0x2F000, fsz=0xD00, entry=0x90,
         # every observed branch target (module offsets); 0x2F010/0x2F340
         # are not auto-detected (no static branch edges to them).
         # NOTE +0x888 = LS 0x2F808: 0x2EF80 + 0x888 (a 0x388 here made the
         # companion probe compute implied base 0x2F480 and never match).
         extras=(0x90, 0x3C0, 0x888, 0x4B0),
         # first-branch companion entries: runtime calls (+0x4B0, +0x888)
         # and internal helpers reached when execution resumes mid-module
         # (+0x90, +0x3C0). One probe per offset.
         probe_entries=(0x4B0, 0x888, 0x90, 0x3C0)),
    dict(name="mstream_dsp_dbg_reverb", base=0x2FD00,
         load=0x2FD80, fsz=0x2180, entry=0xA0,
         extras=(), probe_entries=(0xA0,)),
]

# Image ids (both trees): 14/15 module-relative, 20/21 per-base.
IMG_ID = {"mstream_dsp_dbg_compressor": 14, "mstream_dsp_dbg_reverb": 15}
BASE_IMG_ID = {"mstream_dsp_dbg_compressor": 20, "mstream_dsp_dbg_reverb": 21}

# stale dirs from the superseded (wrong-base) analysis
STALE_DIRS = ["mstream_dsp_dbg_compressor_b2F3A0",
              "mstream_dsp_dbg_reverb_b2FD10"]


def build_pic(load, tail, fsz, entry):
    """Retail-.pic-shaped SPU ELF (ELF32 big-endian, ehdr + 3 phdrs, no
    sections): PT_LOAD at file 0x100 / vaddr 0x80 for fsz bytes, RW bss
    phdr, PT_NOTE of 0x34 bytes at file 0x100+fsz; the dump tail (note +
    .shstrtab names) follows verbatim, mirroring how Sony's .pic files lay
    the note and section-name bytes past the phdr-mapped file range."""
    load_off = 0x100
    note_off = load_off + fsz
    bss_vaddr = (0x80 + fsz + 0x7F) & ~0x7F

    def phdr(t, flags, off, vaddr, filesz, memsz, align):
        return struct.pack(">IIIIIIII", t, off, vaddr, vaddr,
                           filesz, memsz, flags, align)

    ehdr = struct.pack(
        ">16sHHIIIIIHHHHHH",
        bytes((0x7F, 0x45, 0x4C, 0x46, 1, 2, 1)) + b"\0" * 9,
        2, 23, 1,                      # ET_EXEC, EM_SPU, EV_CURRENT
        entry, 52, 0, 0,               # e_entry, e_phoff, e_shoff, e_flags
        52, 32, 3, 0, 0, 0)            # ehsize, phentsize, phnum, sh*
    ph1 = phdr(1, 5, load_off, 0x80, fsz, fsz, 0x80)          # PT_LOAD RX
    ph2 = phdr(1, 6, 0, bss_vaddr, 0, 0x20, 0x80)             # PT_LOAD RW bss
    ph3 = phdr(4, 4, note_off, 0, 0x34, 0, 4)                 # PT_NOTE R
    head = ehdr + ph1 + ph2 + ph3
    assert len(head) <= load_off, len(head)
    head += b"\0" * (load_off - len(head))
    return head + load + tail


def lift(pic, base, prefix, out, extras=()):
    cmd = [sys.executable, LIFTER, "--auto-functions", pic,
           "--base", hex(base), "--symbol-prefix", prefix, "-o", out,
           "--source-name", "spu_recomp.c", "--header-name", "spu_recomp.h"]
    if extras:
        # extra function starts (module vaddrs) the branch scanner cannot
        # see: indirect/runtime-dispatched targets such as compressor+0x4B0
        # (LS 0x2F430) and compressor+0x888 (LS 0x2F808).
        cmd += ["--extra-funcs", ",".join(hex(base + e) for e in extras)]
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    sys.stdout.write("".join("    " + l + "\n" for l in r.stdout.splitlines()))
    if r.returncode != 0:
        sys.stderr.write(r.stderr)
        sys.exit(f"lifter failed for {prefix}")
    return r.stdout


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--dump", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--trees", required=True, help="Comma-separated target-specific output trees")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    trees = [os.path.abspath(t.strip()) for t in args.trees.split(",") if t.strip()]
    if not trees:
        ap.error("--trees must contain at least one output directory")
    dump = open(args.dump, "rb").read()
    os.makedirs(IMAGES_DBG, exist_ok=True)
    for tree in trees:
        for d in STALE_DIRS:
            p = os.path.join(tree, d)
            if os.path.isdir(p):
                shutil.rmtree(p)
                print(f"removed stale dir {p}")

    for m in MODULES:
        lo = m["load"] - DUMP_BASE
        load = dump[lo:lo + m["fsz"]]
        assert len(load) == m["fsz"], m["name"]
        # PT_NOTE + .shstrtab tail: from load end up to the next 0x40-aligned
        # boundary past the section-name block (dump bytes are the file tail).
        tlo = lo + m["fsz"]
        tail = dump[tlo:tlo + 0x44]
        pic = build_pic(load, tail, m["fsz"], m["entry"])
        fnv = fnv1a64(load)
        pic_path = os.path.join(IMAGES_DBG, m["name"] + ".pic")
        with open(pic_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(pic)
        print(f"{m['name']}: base 0x{m['base']:X} fsz 0x{m['fsz']:X} "
              f"entry 0x{m['entry']:X} loadfnv 0x{fnv:016X} "
              f"filefnv 0x{fnv1a64(pic):016X} -> {pic_path}")

        for tree in trees:
            # module-relative lift (identification + any-base interpreter path)
            lift(pic_path, 0, m["name"] + "_",
                 os.path.join(tree, m["name"]), m.get("extras", ()))
            # per-observed-base lift (native dispatch at the logged staging)
            lift(pic_path, m["base"], m["name"] + f"_b{m['base']:X}_",
                 os.path.join(tree, f"{m['name']}_b{m['base']:X}"),
                 m.get("extras", ()))

        img, bimg = IMG_ID[m["name"]], BASE_IMG_ID[m["name"]]
        for entry in m["probe_entries"]:
            if entry == m["probe_entries"][0]:
                vaddr, size = 0x80, m["fsz"]       # primary window
            else:
                # companion: shifted but module-internal window; keeps the
                # (fp, lift_base) dedup pair distinct per entry offset.
                vaddr = 0x80 + 0x20 * m["probe_entries"].index(entry)
                size = m["fsz"] - (vaddr - 0x80)
            win = load[vaddr - 0x80:vaddr - 0x80 + size]
            assert len(win) == size
            # Primary entry gets both the module-relative (interpreter
            # fallback at unseen bases) and the per-base (native) probe;
            # companions are per-base only -- the 16-slot probe table is
            # tight, and unseen-base stagings are covered by the primary
            # module probe for the runtime-call offset.
            lids = ((img, 0x0), (bimg, m["base"])) \
                if entry == m["probe_entries"][0] else ((bimg, m["base"]),)
            for lid, base in lids:
                tag = m["name"] if lid == img else f"{m['name']}@0x{m['base']:X}"
                print(f"    register_stage_probe(0x{fnv1a64(win):016X}ULL, "
                      f"{lid}, 0x{base:X}, 0x{entry:X}, 0x{vaddr:X}, "
                      f"0x{size:X}, \"{tag}+0x{entry:X}\");")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`scripts/spu/lift_ms1_jobmods.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""lift_ms1_jobmods.py -- lift MS1's embedded WWS job binaries and register them.

MS1 embeds its WWS job modules directly in the EBOOT as C0DEC0DE images:

    +0x00  4 x ila marker words        (0x42../0x43.. top byte)
    +0x10  entryOffset                 (u32 BE, from image start)
    +0x14  imageSize                   (u32 BE, == file size)
    +0x18  bssSize                     (the CRT clears [end, end+bssSize))
    +0x20  C0DEC0DE marker
    +0x28  LINK BASE                   (observed 0x4000 on every MS1 image)

The link base is load-bearing: the CRT entry's position probe is
    ila $r2, link+entry+0x38 ; brsl $r126, .+0 ; sf $r126, $r2, $r126
so $r126 (delta) is 0 exactly when the module sits at its link base -- which is
where the img-200 WWS policy module stages it (LS 0x4000, entry 0x4000+entryOff).
A naive base-0 lift makes every absolute ila/lqa immediate wrong by the link
base, and the module-relative seed windows reject all of them, so the lift
silently misses whole functions. Lifting AT the link base (header excluded, so
the header's metadata words cannot masquerade as a function-pointer table) makes
every static address in the lifted C the staged local-store address.

Registration: spu_workload_dispatch_job stages C0DEC0DE images at LS 0, which is
NOT their link base, so that path cannot serve them (a 0x4000-linked binary's
absolute refs would all miss). The PM path is the real one: the policy module
GETs the image into LS 0x4000.. in 0x4000-byte bursts, the runtime's
[pm-jobmod] staging hook (spu_channels.c spu_overlay_note_get) FNV-hashes the
staged bytes and looks the image up here. The PM stages imageSize-0x20 bytes
(the image minus its 0x20-byte trailer -- verified against a live staging of
0x12540 bytes from a 0x12560-byte image), so each module registers under
fnv64(raw[:imageSize-0x20]) with its lifted CRT entry, tagged with the lift base
so the hook's resolver translation is exact:

    spu_workload_register_img_at(fnv64, <prefix>spu_func_<entry>, 210+i,
                                 LINK_BASE, name)

Vendor seed heuristics (first function at +0x30, ila+a link-register targets,
switch tables) are reused with their imm_base (absolute-window) mode, plus two
C0DEC0DE-specific seeders: delta-relocated pointer tables named by
`ila $rT, tbl ; a $rT, $rT, $r126` (the CRT's ctor/dtor walks dispatch through
them; no branch ever names their entries), and an explicit code/data boundary
(--code-end) derived from the const tail so data words that decode as branches
cannot seed phantom functions (5 `.word` failures on the mstream module without
it).

Usage:
    python lift_ms1_jobmods.py [--jobmods DIR] [--out DIR] [--register FILE]
                               [--register-fn NAME]
"""
import argparse, glob, hashlib, json, os, struct, subprocess, sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TOOLS = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "vendor", "ps3recomp", "tools"))
sys.path.insert(0, TOOLS)
from wrap_spu_elf import wrap                       # noqa: E402
from lift_jobmods import manual_link_targets, switch_table_targets  # noqa: E402

LIFTER = os.path.join(TOOLS, "spu_lifter.py")
IMAGE_BASE = 210           # 200 is the wwsjob PM itself; jobmods must not share
                           # its id or spu_lookup dispatches the wrong program's
                           # function at the same LS address.


def fnv1a64(b):
    h = 1469598103934665603
    for x in b:
        h = ((h ^ x) * 1099511628211) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def parse_header(raw, path):
    """Validate the C0DEC0DE image header and return (entry_off, size, link)."""
    if len(raw) < 0x30:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: too small for a C0DEC0DE image header")
    entry_off, size, bss = struct.unpack_from(">III", raw, 0x10)
    link = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, 0x28)[0]
    if raw[0x20:0x24] != b"\xC0\xDE\xC0\xDE":
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no C0DEC0DE marker at +0x20")
    if size != len(raw):
        sys.exit(f"{path}: header imageSize 0x{size:X} != file size 0x{len(raw):X}")
    if raw[0] not in (0x42, 0x43):
        sys.exit(f"{path}: leading word is not an ila marker")
    if link == 0 or link % 0x400 != 0:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: implausible link base 0x{link:X} at +0x28")
    return entry_off, size, link


def data_tail_boundary(raw, link, floor_addr, ptr_values=()):
    """Find the start of the trailing const/data region, as a link-base LS
    address, by scanning words from the image end backward while they are all
    "data-like": zeros, -1 sentinels, ascending byte ladders (prev-w ==
    0x04040404), shuffle masks, float constants, small integers that cannot be
    code addresses at this link base, or code pointers stored in a table
    (ptr_values: the CRT's ctor/dtor tables hold real function addresses, but
    they sit between -1 sentinels in the tail, so the surrounding data -- not
    the pointed-to code -- owns them). Real code is dense with non-constant
    instruction words, so the first code word walking back stops the scan.

    Returns 0 when no run of at least 0x40 bytes qualifies (no cap): the cap
    must never cut an address at or below floor_addr (the highest address any
    deliberate seed named)."""
    def data_like(w, prev):
        if w in (0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80808080):
            return True
        if prev is not None and (prev - w) & 0xFFFFFFFF == 0x04040404:
            return True                      # 00010203/04050607/... ladder
        if not (w & 0x80000000) and 0x38000000 <= (w & 0x7F800000) <= 0x47000000:
            return True                      # float constants (~1.4e-3 .. 3e4)
        if w < link + 0x30:
            return True                      # cannot be code at this link base
        if w in ptr_values:
            return True                      # function pointer inside a table
        return False

    run_end = len(raw) & ~3
    i = run_end - 4
    prev = None
    while i >= 0x30:
        w = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, i)[0]
        if not data_like(w, prev):
            break
        prev = w
        i -= 4
    run_start = i + 4
    if run_end - run_start >= 0x40:
        boundary = link + run_start
        if boundary > floor_addr:
            return boundary
    return 0


def relocated_table_targets(raw, link):
    """Entries of delta-relocated pointer tables. The CRT (and C++ code) walks
    tables of absolute-at-link-base code pointers reached via
        ila $rT, tbl ; a $rT, $rT, $r126   ($r126 = delta, 0 at the link base)
        lqd/rotqby <entry> ; a $r3, $r3, $r126 ; bisl $r0, $r3
    No branch or link-register pattern ever names the entries, so every code
    scanner misses them. Scan a bounded window around each ila-named table base
    for words that are plausible code addresses at the link base. A stray seed
    is harmless (spu_lifter only splits a function that really spans it); a
    missing ctor/dtor entry is a dispatch-to-nothing at run time."""
    out = set()
    for off in range(0x30, len(raw) - 8, 4):
        w = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, off)[0]
        if (w >> 25) & 0x7F != 0x21:                      # ila $rT, i18
            continue
        imm = (w >> 7) & 0x3FFFF
        rt = w & 0x7F
        if not (link + 0x30 <= imm < link + len(raw)):
            continue
        w2 = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, off + 4)[0]
        if (w2 >> 21) & 0x7FF != 0x0C0:                   # a $rT, $rT, $rX
            continue
        if (w2 & 0x7F) != rt or ((w2 >> 7) & 0x7F) != rt:
            continue
        fo = imm - link                                   # table file offset
        for o in range(max(0x30, fo - 0x10), min(len(raw), fo + 0x40), 4):
            v = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, o)[0]
            if v % 4 == 0 and link + 0x30 <= v < link + len(raw):
                out.add(v)
    return sorted(out)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--jobmods", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--register", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--register-fn", default="ms1_jobmods_register_all")
    ap.add_argument("--meta", default=None,
                    help="jobmod_meta.json with stable registration ids and "
                         "pretty names (default: <jobmods>/../jobmod_meta.json). "
                         "Ids never renumber: live logs and the knowledge base "
                         "reference them; newly registrable modules append "
                         "after the highest assigned id and the file is "
                         "updated in place.")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    register_c = args.register or os.path.join(args.out, "jobmods_register.c")
    meta_path = args.meta or os.path.normpath(
        os.path.join(args.jobmods, "..", "jobmod_meta.json"))
    meta = {"ids": {}, "names": {}}
    if os.path.exists(meta_path):
        with open(meta_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            meta = json.load(f)
        meta.setdefault("ids", {}), meta.setdefault("names", {})

    mods = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(args.jobmods, "jobmod_*.bin")))
    if not mods:
        sys.exit(f"no jobmod_*.bin in {args.jobmods}")
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    manifest = []
    tmp_elf = os.path.join(args.out, "_tmp.elf")
    for path in mods:
        raw = open(path, "rb").read()
        name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
        reg_name = meta["names"].get(name, name)
        entry_off, image_size, link = parse_header(raw, path)
        entry = link + entry_off
        base = link + 0x30                     # code starts after the 0x30 hdr
        prefix = f"{name}_"
        outsub = os.path.join(args.out, name)

        seeds = {base}                                   # first function at +0x30
        seeds |= set(manual_link_targets(raw, imm_base=link))
        seeds |= set(switch_table_targets(raw, imm_base=link))
        tbl = set(relocated_table_targets(raw, link))
        seeds |= tbl
        code_end = data_tail_boundary(raw, link, max(seeds | {entry}), tbl)
        if code_end:
            seeds = {s for s in seeds if s < code_end}

        # Wrap MODULE-RELATIVE (PT_LOAD vaddr 0): the lifter shifts
        # auto-detected bounds by --base (contract: "module vaddr 0 lands at
        # LS B"), so an absolute-vaddr wrap here would double-shift every
        # detected function (observed: 2 of 139 bounds kept -- the manual
        # seeds only -- the rest died at the code-end cap). e_entry is
        # likewise wrap-space: the image start (LS link) sits at -0x30 here
        # because the wrap payload starts at image+0x30, so an entryOff
        # passed raw lands 0x30 high and the true CRT entry never lifts
        # (undefined symbol in jobmods_register.c).
        elf = wrap(raw[0x30:image_size], base=0, entry=entry_off - 0x30)
        with open(tmp_elf, "wb") as f:
            f.write(elf)
        cmd = [sys.executable, LIFTER, "--auto-functions", tmp_elf,
               "--base", hex(base), "--symbol-prefix", prefix, "-o", outsub,
               "--source-name", "spu_recomp.c", "--header-name", "spu_recomp.h",
               "--extra-funcs", ",".join(hex(a) for a in sorted(seeds)),
               # undecodable .word slots are data-in-text (ASCII strings the
               # linker placed between functions): guarded, not blocking
               "--data-in-text"]
        if code_end:
            cmd += ["--code-end", hex(code_end)]
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print(f"  FAIL {name}\n{r.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        funcs = unsup = data_words = 0
        for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
            s = line.strip()
            if s.endswith("function(s) lifted"):
                funcs = int(s.split()[0])
            if "unsupported instruction(s)" in s:
                unsup = int(s.split()[0])
            if "data-in-text word(s)" in s:
                data_words = int(s.split()[0])
        manifest.append({"name": name, "reg_name": reg_name,
                         "prefix": prefix, "link_base": link,
                         "entry": entry, "image_size": image_size,
                         "code_end": code_end,
                         "staged_fnv": fnv1a64(raw[:image_size - 0x20]),
                         "funcs": funcs, "unsupported": unsup,
                         "data_words": data_words})
        flag = "  <-- UNSUPPORTED (left unregistered)" if unsup else ""
        print(f"  {name:40} [{reg_name}] funcs={funcs:3} unsup={unsup:3} "
              f"datawords={data_words:3} link=0x{link:X} "
              f"entry=0x{entry:X} code_end="
              f"{'0x%X' % code_end if code_end else '-'}{flag}")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_elf):
        os.remove(tmp_elf)

    with open(os.path.join(args.out, "jobmods_manifest.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

    clean = [m for m in manifest if m["unsupported"] == 0]
    # Stable ids: meta ids win; new registrants append after the highest one.
    used = set(meta["ids"].values())
    nxt = max(used | {IMAGE_BASE - 1})
    for m in clean:
        if m["name"] in meta["ids"]:
            m["id"] = meta["ids"][m["name"]]
            continue
        nxt += 1
        while nxt in used:
            nxt += 1
        m["id"] = nxt
        meta["ids"][m["name"]] = nxt
        used.add(nxt)
        print(f"  new image id {nxt}: {m['name']} [{m['reg_name']}]")
    with open(meta_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")
    L = []
    L.append("/* jobmods_register.c -- GENERATED by recomp/spu/lift_ms1_jobmods.py.")
    L.append(" * MS1's WWS job binaries (C0DEC0DE images, raw bytes under")
    L.append(" * the --jobmods dir, fingerprints in jobmods_manifest.json).")
    L.append(" * Each image is linked at the base declared at header +0x28")
    L.append(" * (0x4000) and the WWS policy module stages it right there, so")
    L.append(" * the lift uses those very addresses and the staging hook's")
    L.append(" * resolver needs no translation. Registered under the FNV-1a-64")
    L.append(" * of the staged span (imageSize-0x20 bytes): what")
    L.append(" * spu_overlay_note_get's [pm-jobmod] accumulator hashes.")
    L.append(" * Image ids are STABLE (jobmod_meta.json): live logs and the")
    L.append(" * knowledge base reference them; new modules append, never")
    L.append(" * renumber. Registration names are the module's real name when")
    L.append(" * identified (debug EBOOT symtab _binary_*_wwsjob_image_start),")
    L.append(" * else the hash stem. Undecodable .word slots are data-in-text")
    L.append(" * constants: guarded, not registration-blocking. */")
    L.append('#include "spu_workload.h"')
    L.append("")
    L.append("extern void spu_begin_image(int image_id);")
    L.append("")
    for m in clean:
        L.append(f"extern void {m['prefix']}spu_func_{m['entry']:08X}(spu_context*);")
        L.append(f"extern void {m['prefix']}spu_recomp_register(void);")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"void {args.register_fn}(void)")
    L.append("{")
    for m in clean:
        img = m["id"]
        L.append(f"    spu_begin_image({img}); {m['prefix']}spu_recomp_register();")
        L.append(f"    spu_workload_register_img_at(0x{m['staged_fnv']:016X}ULL, "
                 f"{m['prefix']}spu_func_{m['entry']:08X}, {img}, "
                 f"0x{m['link_base']:X}u, \"{m['reg_name']}\");")
    L.append("}")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"__attribute__((constructor)) static void {args.register_fn}_ctor(void)")
    L.append("{")
    L.append(f"    {args.register_fn}();")
    L.append("}")
    L.append("")
    with open(register_c, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(L))
    skipped = len(manifest) - len(clean)
    print(f"\nLifted {len(manifest)} module(s); registered {len(clean)} "
          f"({skipped} left unregistered: unsupported instructions -- the "
          f"interpreter keeps serving those); register: {register_c}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`src/diagnostics/bike_capture.h`:

```h
/* Temporary bike-lane observer for issue #24. No guest writes or behavioral
 * substitutions; reads guest memory only through the documented probe helpers.
 * All output is gated on CAP_BIKE_DIR so probe-off boots are unchanged. */
#ifndef BIKE_CAPTURE_H
#define BIKE_CAPTURE_H
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <mutex>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* One ledger across translation units; all mutations are protected. */
struct bike_probe_ledger {
    std::mutex mutex;
    std::map<std::string, unsigned> stages;
    unsigned events = 0;
    bool armed_reported = false;
    bool full_reported = false;
};
inline bike_probe_ledger bike_probe_counts;

static bool bike_probe_read(uint32_t ea, void* dst, size_t len)
{
    SIZE_T read = 0;
    return ea && (uint64_t)ea + len <= 0x100000000ULL &&
        ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess(), vm_base + ea, dst, len, &read) && read == len;
}

static uint32_t bike_probe_word(uint32_t ea)
{
    unsigned char b[4] = {};
    if (!bike_probe_read(ea, b, 4)) return 0;
    return ((uint32_t)b[0]<<24)|((uint32_t)b[1]<<16)|((uint32_t)b[2]<<8)|b[3];
}

static void bike_probe_string(FILE* f, const char* label, uint32_t ea)
{
    char str[129] = {};
    if (ea) {
        for (unsigned i=0; i<128; ++i) {
            if (!bike_probe_read(ea+i, str+i, 1) || !str[i]) break;
            if ((unsigned char)str[i]<32 || (unsigned char)str[i]>126) str[i]='?';
        }
    }
    fprintf(f, "string %s ea=%08X value=%s\n", label, ea, ea ? str : "(null)");
}

static void bike_probe_dump(FILE* f, const char* label, uint32_t ea, size_t len)
{
    if (!ea || !len || len > 4096) return;
    unsigned char bytes[4096];
    bool ok = bike_probe_read(ea, bytes, len);
    fprintf(f, "dump %s ea=%08X size=%zu readable=%d\n", label, ea, len, ok);
    if (ok) {
        for (size_t i=0; i<len; i+=32) {
            fprintf(f, "  %08X:", (uint32_t)(ea+i));
            for (size_t j=0; j<32 && i+j<len; ++j) fprintf(f, " %02X", bytes[i+j]);
            fputc('\n', f);
        }
    }
}

/* Entry probe: one file per event, registers plus selected argument memory.
 * Per-stage and global quotas bound output; exhaustion is explicit. */
static void bike_probe_entry(ppu_context* ctx, const char* stage)
{
    const char* dir = getenv("CAP_BIKE_DIR");
    if (!dir || !*dir || !ctx || !stage || !*stage) return;
    /* Operators create this marker before an observed selection input. Direct
     * users may omit it to capture from boot; no wall-time guess gates events. */
    const char* arm = getenv("CAP_BIKE_ARM_FILE");
    if (arm && *arm && GetFileAttributesA(arm) == INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) return;
    unsigned event;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(bike_probe_counts.mutex);
        auto& ledger = bike_probe_counts;
        if (!ledger.armed_reported) {
            ledger.armed_reported = true;
            fprintf(stderr, "[DEBUG-bike-oct11] armed dir=%s\n", dir);
        }
        if (ledger.events >= 1024 ||
            (ledger.stages.size() >= 32 && !ledger.stages.count(stage))) {
            if (!ledger.full_reported) {
                ledger.full_reported = true;
                fprintf(stderr, "[DEBUG-bike-oct11] global capture budget reached\n");
            }
            return;
        }
        unsigned& count = ledger.stages[stage];
        if (count >= 64) return;
        if (++count == 64)
            fprintf(stderr, "[DEBUG-bike-oct11] stage=%s capture budget reached\n", stage);
        event = ledger.events++;
    }
    char path[1024];
    snprintf(path,sizeof(path),"%s/%04u_%s.txt",dir,event,stage);
    FILE* f=fopen(path,"wb");
    if (!f) { fprintf(stderr,"[DEBUG-bike-oct11] capture fopen failed path=%s errno=%d\n",path,errno); return; }
    fprintf(f,"stage=%s thread=%lu tick=%llu lr=%08llX\n",stage,
            GetCurrentThreadId(),(unsigned long long)GetTickCount64(),ctx->lr);
    for (unsigned i=0;i<32;++i) fprintf(f,"r%u=%016llX\n",i,ctx->gpr[i]);
    if (!strcmp(stage,"vpfn") || !strcmp(stage,"dynsel") || !strcmp(stage,"rsload")) {
        bike_probe_string(f,"name",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4]);
    }
    if (!strcmp(stage,"rsfind")) {
        /* ResourceIdentifier blob (r4): dump raw so its layout is observable. */
        bike_probe_dump(f,"identifier",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4],96);
    }
    if (!strcmp(stage,"sor") || !strcmp(stage,"vtload")) {
        /* this=r3, resource system=r4, stream=r5; dump stream header. */
        bike_probe_dump(f,"stream",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5],192);
        uint32_t vtable=bike_probe_word((uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5]);
        bike_probe_dump(f,"stream_vtable",vtable,128);
    }
    if (!strcmp(stage,"sor")) {
        /* SceneObjectResource base resource fields after the fact. */
        bike_probe_dump(f,"resourcesystem",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4],64);
    }
    if (ferror(f)) fprintf(stderr,"[DEBUG-bike-oct11] capture write failed path=%s\n",path);
    if (fclose(f)) fprintf(stderr,"[DEBUG-bike-oct11] capture close failed path=%s errno=%d\n",path,errno);
    fprintf(stderr,"[DEBUG-bike-oct11] event=%u stage=%s\n",event,stage);
}

#endif
```

`src/diagnostics/havok_capture.h`:

```h
/* Temporary named-build observer. No guest writes or behavioral substitutions. */
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <atomic>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static std::atomic<unsigned> havok_probe_events{0};
static std::atomic<size_t> havok_probe_bytes{0};
static thread_local unsigned havok_probe_id;
static thread_local uint32_t havok_probe_stream;
static std::atomic<unsigned> havok_raw_slots{0};
static thread_local unsigned char* havok_raw_bytes;
static thread_local size_t havok_raw_length;
static thread_local uint32_t havok_raw_object;
static thread_local uint32_t havok_raw_ea;
static thread_local uint32_t havok_raw_stream;
static thread_local uint32_t havok_raw_site;

static bool havok_probe_read(uint32_t ea, void* dst, size_t len)
{
    SIZE_T read = 0;
    return (uint64_t)ea + len <= 0x100000000ULL &&
        ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess(), vm_base + ea, dst, len, &read) && read == len;
}

static uint32_t havok_probe_word(uint32_t ea)
{
    unsigned char b[4] = {};
    if (!havok_probe_read(ea, b, 4)) return 0;
    return ((uint32_t)b[0]<<24)|((uint32_t)b[1]<<16)|((uint32_t)b[2]<<8)|b[3];
}

/* Private diagnostic cache: max four16MiB host buffers, no disk/log on success. */
static void havok_record_raw_oct10(ppu_context* ctx, uint32_t site = 0)
{
    (void)site;
    havok_raw_length=0;
    if (!getenv("CAP_HAVOK_DIR")) return;
    uint32_t object=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[20];
    uint32_t length=havok_probe_word(object+0x20);
    if (!length || length>16*1024*1024) return;
    if (!havok_raw_bytes && havok_raw_slots.fetch_add(1)<4)
        havok_raw_bytes=(unsigned char*)malloc(16*1024*1024);
    if (!havok_raw_bytes) return;
    havok_raw_object=object;havok_raw_ea=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[31];
    havok_raw_stream=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[30];havok_raw_site=site;
    if (havok_probe_read(havok_raw_ea,havok_raw_bytes,length)) havok_raw_length=length;
}

static void havok_probe_dump(FILE* meta, const char* dir, unsigned event,
                             const char* label, uint32_t ea, size_t len)
{
    if (!len || len > 16*1024*1024) return;
    size_t before = havok_probe_bytes.fetch_add(len);
    if (before + len > 128*1024*1024) return;
    unsigned char* bytes = (unsigned char*)malloc(len);
    bool ok = bytes && havok_probe_read(ea, bytes, len);
    fprintf(meta, "dump %s ea=%08X size=%zu readable=%d\n", label, ea, len, ok);
    if (ok) {
        char path[1024];
        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%04u_%s_%08X.bin", dir, event, label, ea);
        FILE* f = fopen(path, "wb");
        if (f) { fwrite(bytes, 1, len, f); fclose(f); }
    }
    free(bytes);
}

static void havok_probe_string(FILE* meta, const char* label, uint32_t ea)
{
    if (!ea) { fprintf(meta,"string %s ea=00000000 value=<null>\n",label); return; }
    char str[257] = {};
    for (unsigned i=0; i<256; ++i) {
        if (!havok_probe_read(ea+i, str+i, 1) || !str[i]) break;
        if ((unsigned char)str[i]<32 || (unsigned char)str[i]>126) str[i]='?';
    }
    fprintf(meta, "string %s ea=%08X value=%s\n", label, ea, str);
}

static void havok_probe_oct10(ppu_context* ctx, const char* stage, uint32_t site = 0)
{
    (void)site;
    const char* dir = getenv("CAP_HAVOK_DIR");
    if (!dir || !*dir) return;
    unsigned event = havok_probe_events.fetch_add(1);
    if (event>=128) return;
    if (!strcmp(stage, "entry")) {
        havok_probe_id=event;
        havok_probe_stream=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5];
    }
    char path[1024];
    snprintf(path,sizeof(path),"%s/%04u_%s.txt",dir,event,stage);
    FILE* f=fopen(path,"wb");
    if (!f) return;
    fprintf(f,"stage=%s ctor=%u thread=%lu tick=%llu lr=%08llX\n",stage,havok_probe_id,
            GetCurrentThreadId(),(unsigned long long)GetTickCount64(),ctx->lr);
    for (unsigned i=0;i<32;++i) fprintf(f,"r%u=%016llX\n",i,ctx->gpr[i]);
    fprintf(f,"observer_site=%08X raw_site=%08X (explicit hook sites, not LR/CIA-derived PCs)\n",site,havok_raw_site);
    if (!strcmp(stage,"fatal177")) {
        fprintf(f,"raw_cache object=%08X ea=%08X length=%zu matches=%d\n",
                havok_raw_object,havok_raw_ea,havok_raw_length,
                havok_raw_object==(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[20]);
        uint32_t object=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[20];
        fprintf(f,"resource_id=%08X%08X\n",havok_probe_word(object+0x10),havok_probe_word(object+0x14));
        fprintf(f,"raw_stream=%08X\n",havok_raw_stream);
        if (havok_raw_object==object) {
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"raw_stream",havok_raw_stream,256);
            for (unsigned i=0;i<16;++i) {
                uint32_t ptr=havok_probe_word(havok_raw_stream+4*i);
                char label[32];snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"stream_ptr%u",i);
                if (ptr) havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,label,ptr,256);
            }
        }
        if (havok_raw_length && havok_raw_object==(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[20]) {
            char raw_path[1024];
            snprintf(raw_path,sizeof(raw_path),"%s/%04u_pre_relocation_%08X.bin",dir,event,havok_raw_ea);
            FILE* raw=fopen(raw_path,"wb");
            if (raw) { fwrite(havok_raw_bytes,1,havok_raw_length,raw);fclose(raw); }
        }
    }
    havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"stack",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[1],4096);
    havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"stream",havok_probe_stream,256);
    if (!strcmp(stage,"entry")) {
        for (unsigned i=0;i<16;++i) {
            char label[32];snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"stream_ptr%u",i);
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,label,havok_probe_word(havok_probe_stream+4*i),256);
        }
    } else {
        uint32_t object=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[20];
        havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"resource",object,128);
        uint32_t data=havok_probe_word(object+0x24);
        uint32_t len=havok_probe_word(object+0x20);
        havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"packfile",data,len);
        if (!strcmp(stage,"raw"))
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"aligned_stream_bytes",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[31],len);
        if (strcmp(stage,"raw")) {
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"result",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[22],32);
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"reader",(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[25],128);
            uint32_t root=(uint32_t)ctx->gpr[24];
            havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"root",root,64);
            uint32_t variants=havok_probe_word(root);
            uint32_t count=havok_probe_word(root+4);
            fprintf(f,"root=%08X variants=%08X count=%u\n",root,variants,count);
            if (count<=64) {
                havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,"variants",variants,16*count);
                for (unsigned i=0;i<count;++i) {
                    uint32_t v=variants+16*i;
                    char label[32];snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"name%u",i);
                    havok_probe_string(f,label,havok_probe_word(v));
                    snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"class%u",i);
                    havok_probe_string(f,label,havok_probe_word(v+4));
                    snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"variant%u",i);
                    havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,label,havok_probe_word(v+8),256);
                }
            }
            for (unsigned offset=0x5750;offset<=0x575C;offset+=4) {
                char label[32];snprintf(label,sizeof(label),"class_toc_%X",offset);
                havok_probe_dump(f,dir,event,label,havok_probe_word((uint32_t)ctx->gpr[2]+offset),128);
            }
        }
    }
    fclose(f);
    fprintf(stderr,"[DEBUG-havok-oct10] event=%u ctor=%u stage=%s\n",event,havok_probe_id,stage);
}
```

`src/main.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * ps3recomp game project -- entry point template.
 *
 * This is the runner. It boots a lifted title through the toolkit's PPU
 * scaffold: allocate the flat guest VM, load the PPU ELF named on the command
 * line, register the lifted function table and the HLE NID handlers, start a
 * frame clock, and dispatch the entry OPD.
 *
 * The scaffold does the work; nothing below reimplements it. ppu_load_elf,
 * ppu_recomp_register, ppu_hle_init, ppu_sysprx_register, ppu_fs_register,
 * lv2_init_syscalls and ppu_run all come from the toolkit, compiled into this
 * project from PS3RECOMP_DIR (see CMakeLists.txt). What is left here is the
 * part a port owns: which backend to present through, how the frame clock is
 * paced, and whatever diagnostics the title turns out to need.
 *
 * runtime/ppu/tests/boot_main.cpp in the toolkit is the same boot in its
 * fully-instrumented form -- crash filter, hang watchdog, guest-PC sampling
 * profiler. Read it when a boot goes wrong; copy from it what the title
 * needs. It is deliberately not what a fresh project starts with.
 *
 * The one part that IS duplicated from it is the frame clock below, because a
 * port is expected to change its pacing and a shared one would be the wrong
 * shape for that. It was copied faithfully, comments and all. If a pacing bug
 * is fixed in one of the two, look at the other.
 *
 * This builds on Windows, macOS and Linux. CI builds and runs it against the
 * boot smoke title on the last two, and compile-checks it against clang-cl on
 * the first (tools/check_ppu_scaffold.py).
 */

/* The lifter's generated header, which declares ppu_context and the function
 * table. It comes first: everything below is written against that struct. */
#include "ppu_recomp.h"

/* The Win32 names -- Sleep, GetTickCount64, CreateThread, InterlockedIncrement,
 * VirtualAlloc, the scalar typedefs -- from one place. On Windows this is a
 * passthrough to <windows.h>; off Windows the toolkit's shim supplies the same
 * names over pthreads and mmap, so the call sites below are written once. */
#include "win32_compat.h"
#include "thread_name.h"   /* ps3_thread_setname */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#ifdef _WIN32
/* timeBeginPeriod: <windows.h> arrives with WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN set, which
 * excludes the multimedia timer API, so it is asked for by name -- and after
 * windows.h, since timeapi.h uses UINT. No shim exists off Windows because
 * there is nothing to shim: the 15.6 ms default timer granularity this works
 * around is a Windows problem. */
#include <timeapi.h>
#endif

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * What the scaffold gives this file
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
extern "C" {
uint32_t ppu_load_elf(const char* path);      /* ELF -> guest RAM, returns entry OPD */
void     ppu_recomp_register(void);           /* generated: lifted table -> address map */
void     ppu_hle_init(void);                  /* firmware import NID -> HLE handler */
void     ppu_sysprx_register(void);           /* boot-critical CRT (sys_initialize_tls, ...) */
void     ppu_fs_register(void);               /* cellFs over the real game directory */
void     lv2_init_syscalls(void);             /* the lv2 syscall table */
int      ppu_run(uint32_t entry_opd, uint32_t stack_top);

/* This project's own: load whatever real system PRX modules the title needs
 * into guest RAM and register their exports. stubs.cpp has the empty version
 * a game with no lifted PRX wants. */
void     ps3_load_prx_modules(void);

extern const char* ppu_vfs_root;              /* host dir the PS3 mount points map into */

/* The status the guest handed to sys_process_exit. A title that exits that way
 * never returns through ppu_run, so this is only read on the path where the
 * entry function unwound instead. */
extern int     g_sys_process_exit_called;
extern int32_t g_sys_process_exit_code;

/* Host-provided symbols the runtime and the HLE libraries link against. */
uint8_t* vm_base = nullptr;
extern uint32_t ppu_vm_size;                  /* ppu_loader.cpp: the OOB guard */

/* Guest-callback dispatch. g_ps3_guest_caller is the hook the HLE runtime
 * calls back into recompiled code through -- cellSysutil events and the GCM
 * vblank/flip handlers. ppu_guest_call does the OPD -> dispatch. */
typedef void (*ps3_guest_caller_fn)(uint32_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t,
                                    uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t);
extern ps3_guest_caller_fn g_ps3_guest_caller;
uint64_t ppu_guest_call(uint32_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t,
                        uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t);

/* The GCM half of the frame clock. */
void     cellGcmTickVBlank(void);
void     cellGcmTickFlip(void);
int      cellGcm_take_flip_pending_synced(void);
void     cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo(void);      /* drain get -> put */
unsigned cellGcm_flip_request_count(void);
/* A guest thread whose fence wait found the FIFO dry sets this; waiting on it
 * here instead of a blind sleep services fence/label polls at ~0ms latency. */
void*    cellGcm_fifo_kick_event(void);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * RSX present backend
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* D3D12 on Windows, Metal on Apple, and the null backend's headless software
 * path anywhere else -- the same selection runtime/host/host_posix.c and the
 * toolkit's boot harness make. All three expose the same three entry points,
 * so the frame clock below is backend-agnostic. */
#if defined(_WIN32)
extern "C" int  rsx_d3d12_backend_init(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, const char* title);
extern "C" void rsx_d3d12_backend_present(void);
extern "C" int  rsx_d3d12_backend_pump_messages(void);
#  define rsx_backend_init    rsx_d3d12_backend_init
#  define rsx_backend_present rsx_d3d12_backend_present
#  define rsx_backend_pump    rsx_d3d12_backend_pump_messages
#  define RSX_BACKEND_NAME    "D3D12"
#elif defined(__APPLE__)
extern "C" int  rsx_metal_backend_init(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, const char* title);
extern "C" void rsx_metal_backend_present(void);
extern "C" int  rsx_metal_backend_pump_messages(void);
#  define rsx_backend_init    rsx_metal_backend_init
#  define rsx_backend_present rsx_metal_backend_present
#  define rsx_backend_pump    rsx_metal_backend_pump_messages
#  define RSX_BACKEND_NAME    "Metal"
#else
extern "C" int  rsx_null_backend_init(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, const char* title);
extern "C" void rsx_null_backend_present(void);
extern "C" int  rsx_null_backend_pump_messages(void);
#  define rsx_backend_init    rsx_null_backend_init
#  define rsx_backend_present rsx_null_backend_present
#  define rsx_backend_pump    rsx_null_backend_pump_messages
#  define RSX_BACKEND_NAME    "null (headless software)"
#endif

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Configuration
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* The flat VM must span every region the PS3 memory map uses, not just the
 * game image: sys_ppu_thread_create puts thread stacks at 0xD0000000, so a
 * smaller arena makes every spawned thread's stack access out of bounds. */
#define VM_SIZE       0x100010000ull   /* the full 32-bit guest space + a 64K guard */
#define STACK_TOP     0x0FF00000u      /* main-thread stack, below the 0x10000000 segment */
#define WINDOW_WIDTH  1280
#define WINDOW_HEIGHT 720

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Frame clock
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* On real hardware the RSX raises a vblank interrupt about 60 times a second
 * and that is what drives the game's frame loop. With no RSX it is synthesized
 * here: a host thread calls cellGcmTickVBlank/TickFlip, which invoke the
 * handlers the guest registered, and drains the GCM FIFO. Without this the
 * title initialises, registers its handlers and then waits forever.
 *
 * The ticks are driven off real elapsed time rather than off how long present()
 * took: a hidden or occluded window makes present block hard, and pacing the
 * ticks behind it paces the whole game behind it. The loop runs at a fast
 * (~1 ms) cadence so the FIFO drain -- the thing every guest fence and label
 * poll waits on -- never waits a 16 ms beat, while vblank/flip completions
 * fire only on the 59.94 Hz beats. */
static volatile LONG g_frames_presented = 0;

/* Frames handed to the backend at a guest FLIP boundary -- one per frame the
 * guest actually finished. The presents made before the guest's first flip, so
 * a fresh window is not left blank through a long boot, carry no guest frame
 * and are deliberately not counted. */
extern "C" unsigned ppu_boot_frames_presented(void)
{
    return (unsigned)g_frames_presented;
}

static void present_guest_frame(void)
{
    rsx_backend_present();
    /* This thread increments and guest threads read, so interlocked rather
     * than a volatile ++, which on arm64 is neither atomic nor a fence. */
    InterlockedIncrement(&g_frames_presented);
}

/* One fast-cadence iteration of the frame loop: pump window messages, drain
 * the FIFO, present a completed flip. Returns 0 when the window died; the
 * caller then stops touching the backend but keeps the vblank beats going,
 * so the guest does not hang behind a closed window. */
static int frame_clock_iteration(int rsx_ok)
{
    if (!rsx_ok) return 1;
    if (rsx_backend_pump() != 0) return 0;
    /* Drain FIRST, at the fast (~1 ms) cadence: titles fence every render
     * pass on an RSX label the drain writes. At a 16 ms drain each fence
     * cost a frame's worth of time (wave: six passes -> ~7 fps; the
     * MotorStorm menu sat at 13-26 fps with a ~33 ms gap between submits
     * because every wait landed on the next 16 ms beat). */
    cellGcm_rsx_process_fifo();
    /* Present once the drain has consumed the flipped frame:
     * take_flip_pending_synced only fires at get==put, so the batch held is
     * exactly the completed frame (the guest blocks in WaitFlip after
     * flipping). */
    if (cellGcm_take_flip_pending_synced()) {
        present_guest_frame();
        return 1;
    }
    /* Boot fallback: before the first flip, present freely so the window is
     * not left blank through a long boot. */
    if (cellGcm_flip_request_count() == 0) rsx_backend_present();
    return 1;
}

static DWORD WINAPI frame_clock(LPVOID)
{
    const char* title = getenv("PS3_TITLE");
    if (!title || !*title) title = "ps3recomp";

    int rsx_ok = (rsx_backend_init(WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT, title) == 0);
    fprintf(stderr, "[rsx] %s backend init %s\n", RSX_BACKEND_NAME,
            rsx_ok ? "OK -- window open" : "FAILED");


#ifdef _WIN32
    /* Vblank beats at the true PS3 rate (59.94 Hz NTSC), accumulated on QPC.
     * GetTickCount64 + `next_tick += 16` quantized the beat to whole ms at
     * 62.5 Hz, which drifts against the 59.94 Hz vsync present and made every
     * flip-synced title skip beats. Accumulating qpf*1001/60000 QPC ticks
     * holds 60000/1001 Hz to within the period truncation (<=1 tick/beat). */
    LARGE_INTEGER qpf_li, qpc_li;
    QueryPerformanceFrequency(&qpf_li);
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&qpc_li);
    const ULONGLONG vblank_period = (ULONGLONG)(qpf_li.QuadPart * 1001ULL / 60000ULL);
    ULONGLONG next_tick = (ULONGLONG)qpc_li.QuadPart;
    /* High-resolution waitable timer for the fast cadence. Sleep() rounds to
     * the 15.6 ms scheduler tick -- and Windows 10+ ignores timeBeginPeriod
     * for unfocused processes -- which capped the FIFO-drain cadence at
     * ~64 Hz and paced guests into the 13-26 fps range. The
     * HIGH_RESOLUTION flag is precise and focus-independent (Win10 1803+).
     * The kick event is in the wait set: a fence-starved guest wakes the
     * drain immediately instead of after the timer slice. */
    HANDLE hrtimer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL,
        0x00000002 /* CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
    HANDLE kick = (HANDLE)cellGcm_fifo_kick_event();
    HANDLE waits[2]; int n_waits = 0;
    if (hrtimer) waits[n_waits++] = hrtimer;
    if (kick)    waits[n_waits++] = kick;

    for (;;) {
        if (hrtimer) {
            LARGE_INTEGER due; due.QuadPart = -10000;   /* 1 ms, 100 ns units */
            SetWaitableTimer(hrtimer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE);
            WaitForMultipleObjects(n_waits, waits, FALSE, 2);
        } else if (kick) {
            WaitForSingleObject(kick, 2);
        } else {
            Sleep(2);
        }
        QueryPerformanceCounter(&qpc_li);
        ULONGLONG now = (ULONGLONG)qpc_li.QuadPart;
        while ((long long)(now - next_tick) >= 0) {
            cellGcmTickVBlank();
            /* Flip completion on the vblank beat = 59.94 Hz vsync pacing;
             * with the fast fence drain below, an unpaced guest otherwise
             * runs far past 60 fps. */
            cellGcmTickFlip();
            next_tick += vblank_period;
            /* Fell >1 s behind (debugger pause, machine sleep): resync
             * instead of machine-gunning catch-up vblanks. */
            if ((long long)(now - next_tick) > (long long)(qpf_li.QuadPart)) {
                next_tick = now;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!frame_clock_iteration(rsx_ok)) rsx_ok = 0;
    }
#else
    /* POSIX: no waitable-timer API; plain sleeps are already fine-grained.
     * 17 ms whole-ms beats ~= 58.8 Hz (the smoke titles do not pace on it). */
    ULONGLONG next_tick = GetTickCount64();
    for (;;) {
        Sleep(2);
        ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
        while ((long long)(now - next_tick) >= 0) {
            cellGcmTickVBlank();
            cellGcmTickFlip();
            next_tick += 17;
            if ((long long)(now - next_tick) > 1000) { next_tick = now; break; }
        }
        if (!frame_clock_iteration(rsx_ok)) rsx_ok = 0;
    }
#endif
    return 0;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * VFS root
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* Derive the directory holding PS3_GAME from the EBOOT path
 * <root>/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf -> <root>. $PS3_VFS_ROOT overrides. */
static char s_vfs_root[1024];

static void derive_vfs_root(const char* eboot)
{
    const char* env = getenv("PS3_VFS_ROOT");
    if (env && *env) { ppu_vfs_root = env; return; }

    strncpy(s_vfs_root, eboot, sizeof s_vfs_root - 1);
    for (char* p = s_vfs_root; *p; p++) if (*p == '\\') *p = '/';
    /* strip EBOOT.elf, USRDIR and PS3_GAME */
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { char* s = strrchr(s_vfs_root, '/'); if (s) *s = 0; }
    if (!s_vfs_root[0]) strcpy(s_vfs_root, ".");
    ppu_vfs_root = s_vfs_root;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Guest VM
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
#ifdef _WIN32
/* Demand-paging for the flat VM: reserve the whole 4 GB guest space, which
 * costs no commit, and commit each 64 KB page on first access. Every 32-bit
 * guest offset is then valid, so a garbage guest pointer reads zero instead of
 * killing the process. Faults outside the arena fall through untouched. */
static LONG WINAPI vm_commit_veh(EXCEPTION_POINTERS* ep)
{
    if (ep->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionCode == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION) {
        ULONG_PTR fault = ep->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionInformation[1];
        uintptr_t base  = (uintptr_t)vm_base;
        if (vm_base && fault >= base && fault < base + VM_SIZE) {
            void* page = (void*)(fault & ~(uintptr_t)0xFFFF);
            if (VirtualAlloc(page, 0x10000, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE))
                return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
        }
    }
    return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
}
#endif

static bool alloc_guest_vm(void)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, vm_commit_veh);
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)VirtualAlloc(NULL, VM_SIZE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE);
    ppu_vm_size = 0;              /* the whole space is backed; no OOB guard needed */
#else
    /* No vectored exception handlers off Windows, so the arena is committed up
     * front and lazily backed by the OS: only pages the title touches cost
     * anything. It stops below the 0xE0000000 mark, so ppu_vm_size arms the
     * loader's bounds check for what is left. */
    vm_base = (uint8_t*)calloc(1, 0xE0000000u);
    ppu_vm_size = 0xE0000000u;
#endif
    return vm_base != nullptr;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Main
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
static void harness_guest_caller(uint32_t opd, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1,
                                 uint64_t a2, uint64_t a3, uint64_t a4,
                                 uint64_t a5, uint64_t a6, uint64_t a7)
{
    ppu_guest_call(opd, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7);
}

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) {
        printf("usage: %s <PPU ELF>\n", argv[0]);
        return 2;
    }

#ifdef _WIN32
#pragma comment(lib, "winmm.lib")
    /* 1 ms timer resolution. The default granularity is about 15.6 ms, which
     * inflates every shorter wait the title makes and throttles the whole
     * thing. POSIX timers are already fine-grained. */
    timeBeginPeriod(1);
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);   /* unbuffered: do not lose prints on a kill */
#endif

    printf("=== ps3recomp game runner ===\n");

    if (!alloc_guest_vm()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: could not allocate the guest address space\n");
        return 1;
    }

    uint32_t entry = ppu_load_elf(argv[1]);
    if (!entry) {
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: could not load %s\n", argv[1]);
        return 1;
    }

    derive_vfs_root(argv[1]);
    printf("[boot] VFS root: %s\n", ppu_vfs_root);

    /* MotorStorm imports the bare-name sys_net exports (connect, getsockname,
     * send, ...). Only the PS3_NET_ONLINE model registers them; without it
     * every one falls to the unresolved-NID default, which answers CELL_OK
     * with out-params untouched. Sockets that cannot reach PSN fail with
     * honest host errors, which is the offline behavior the game expects. */
    _putenv("PS3_NET_ONLINE=1");

    ppu_recomp_register();   /* lifted function table -> address map */
    ps3_load_prx_modules();  /* this game's lifted system PRX, if it has any */
    ppu_hle_init();          /* firmware import NID -> HLE handlers */
    ppu_sysprx_register();   /* boot-critical CRT */
    ppu_fs_register();       /* cellFs over the game directory */
    lv2_init_syscalls();     /* the lv2 syscall table */

    /* Install the guest-callback hook, then start the frame clock. It no-ops
     * until the title registers its vblank and flip handlers during init. */
    g_ps3_guest_caller = harness_guest_caller;
    { HANDLE _fc = CreateThread(NULL, 4u * 1024 * 1024, frame_clock, NULL, 0, NULL);
      ps3_thread_setname((uintptr_t)_fc, "frame_clock"); }

    printf("\n[boot] dispatching entry OPD 0x%08X (stack top 0x%08X)\n\n",
           entry, STACK_TOP);

    int rc = ppu_run(entry, STACK_TOP);
    printf("\n[boot] ppu_run returned %d (entry function unwound)\n", rc);

    /* A title that called sys_process_exit never reaches this line: that path
     * ends in the host exit(). Getting here means the entry function returned
     * instead, so hand back the status the guest published if it published
     * one. Returning a hardcoded 0 would report success for a run that never
     * got anywhere. */
    return g_sys_process_exit_called ? (int)g_sys_process_exit_code : 0;
}
```

```txt
# Keep in step with the changelog in README.md. This sat at 0.3.0 until August
# 2026 while the project shipped 0.6.x through 0.8.0, so every build printed
# "ps3recomp runtime v0.3.0" and was believed. v0.9.0 is the first TAGGED one.
project(ps3recomp_runtime
    VERSION 0.11.0
    LANGUAGES C CXX
    DESCRIPTION "ps3recomp - Static recompilation runtime for PS3 games"

# Collect source files

# rather than globbed. It needs no platform #ifdef of its own as a result.

# to a stub wherever the shader tools are absent, so it is part of the
# library everywhere. See the "Guest shaders on Metal" section below.
list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libs/video/rsx_shader_msl.cpp")

# (LGPL-2.1, kept separate in third_party/at3_standalone -- see its README).

list(APPEND HLE_SOURCES ${AT3_SOURCES})
```
